x: The thermocline is the layer where temperature falls quickly with depth. Halocline is for salinity and pycnocline for density.
t: Read the prefix: thermo, halo, pycno.

x: Option A is incorrect: the Arabian Sea is about 36‰ because of high evaporation. The Bay of Bengal is about 30‰ from river inflow, and the average is about 35‰.
t: Discriminate the salinity of the two seas.

x: Both are true and R explains A: colder water is denser, so cold water sinks and fills the deep ocean.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: The thermocline is a sharp temperature change, the halocline a sharp salinity change, the pycnocline a sharp density change and isohalines join equal salinity, giving a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i.
t: Read the prefix: thermo, halo, pycno.

x: I, II and IV are correct: the equator is less saline from heavy rain, and the 20°–40° subtropics are most saline from evaporation. III is false because polar seas are less saline from low evaporation and melting ice.
t: Relate salinity to evaporation and fresh water.

x: Option D is incorrect: coral reefs are among the richest ecosystems on Earth. They grow in warm waters of about 25°N–25°S from polyp skeletons.
t: Check for a reversed property.

x: The Brazil Current and Gulf Stream are warm; the Falkland and Labrador currents are cold, giving ii, i, ii, i.
t: Discriminate warm from cold currents.

x: A is true: acidification harms corals and calcareous plankton. B is false because "necessarily" overstates any link with cloud formation.
t: Check for an absolute word like "necessarily".

x: The Great Barrier Reef lies off the Queensland coast of north-east Australia.
t: Recall the location of major reefs.

x: I and II are correct: phytoplankton are producers and zooplankton animal plankton. III and IV are swapped: nekton swim actively and benthos live on the bottom.
t: Check for swapped definitions.

x: All four control ocean currents: differential heating, trade winds, coastline shape and tides.
t: Recall the causes of ocean currents.

x: Both are true and R explains A: by carrying heat from low to high latitudes, currents warm or cool the coasts they pass.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: All five are correct: surface temperature depends on latitude and insolation, falls with depth and affects density, circulation and marine life.
t: Recall the facts of ocean temperature.

x: Both are true: density depends mainly on temperature and salinity, and saltier water is denser.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: Both are true and R explains A: because density rises sharply across the pycnocline, lighter surface water sits stably above denser deep water, so little mixing occurs between them.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.
s: Assertion (A): The pycnocline acts as a barrier that limits vertical mixing between surface water and deep water. Reason (R): The pycnocline is a layer in which density increases rapidly with depth.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true

x: Thermo means temperature, halo salt and pycno density, giving a-iii, b-i, c-ii.
t: Read the prefix: thermo, halo, pycno.

x: All six control salinity: evaporation, precipitation, river water, winds, currents, and the freezing and thawing of ice, which adds or removes fresh water.
t: Count carefully and note option wording.
s: How many of the following are listed as factors controlling ocean salinity? 1. Evaporation 2. Precipitation 3. River water 4. Winds 5. Ocean currents 6. Freezing and thawing of ice

x: Average salinity of 35‰ means 35 g of salts per 1 kg of seawater, measured by mass, not per litre.
t: Read ‰ as parts per thousand by mass.

x: Option B is incorrect: most ocean salt comes from land, carried by rivers. Volcanic activity adds only a smaller share.
t: Discriminate the main source from minor ones.

x: All five are correct: sodium chloride is about 77.8% of dissolved salts, then magnesium chloride 10.9%, magnesium sulphate 4.7%, calcium sulphate 3.6% and potassium sulphate 2.5%.
t: Recall the order of ocean salts.

x: Calcium carbonate is about 0.3%, magnesium bromide 0.2%, calcium sulphate 3.6% and potassium sulphate 2.5%, giving a-iv, b-i, c-ii, d-iii.
t: Recall the order of ocean salts.

x: Both are true and R explains A: high evaporation raises Arabian Sea salinity, while rivers dilute the Bay of Bengal.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: All four are correct: the Red Sea is very saline because of strong evaporation, little rain, few rivers and a narrow link through Bab-el-Mandeb.
t: Relate salinity to evaporation and fresh water.

x: The westerlies drive mid-latitude currents, the Coriolis effect deflects them to the right in the Northern Hemisphere, coastlines block and redirect them, and floor relief steers them along ridges and basins, giving a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i.
t: Recall the controls of ocean currents.
s: Match List-I with List-II: List-I (a) Westerlies (b) Coriolis effect (c) Coastline configuration (d) Ocean-floor relief List-II (i) Steers currents along submarine ridges and basins (ii) Drives mid-latitude currents (iii) Deflects currents to the right in the Northern Hemisphere (iv) Blocks and redirects currents along landmasses

x: Both are true: ocean-floor shape and gravity both control currents.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: The Kuroshio is a warm current off Japan; the Canary is a cold current off north-west Africa.
t: Discriminate warm from cold currents.

x: Both are true: warm currents carry warm water poleward and cold currents carry cold water toward the equator.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: All three are correct: plankton drift with the water, coral reefs are highly diverse, and Australia has a major share of reefs.
t: Count the correct statements carefully.

x: Tides are the periodic rise and fall of sea level caused by the pull of the Moon and Sun. Westerlies drive currents, the Coriolis effect deflects them and floor relief steers them.
t: Discriminate causes from steering factors.
s: Which of the following causes the periodic vertical rise and fall of sea level?

x: All four are correct: Australia, Indonesia and the Philippines hold major coral reefs, and the Great Barrier Reef in Australia is the largest.
t: Recall the location of major reefs.

x: The Great Barrier Reef is in the Pacific, and Addu Atoll in the Maldives is in the Indian Ocean, giving a-i, b-ii.
t: Recall the location of major reefs.

x: All four describe an atoll: a ring or horseshoe coral reef around a lagoon in tropical or subtropical seas.
t: Recall the features of an atoll.

x: Both are true and R explains A: more CO₂ dissolves to form carbonic acid, lowering pH and reducing carbonate.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: Both are true: less carbonate harms shell-building organisms, so some marine life suffers from acidification.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: Both are true and R explains A: Australia is the country near the largest reef because the Great Barrier Reef lies there.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: Both are true and R explains A: coastlines control currents by deflecting them.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: Coral reefs are mainly in tropical and semi-tropical waters, around 25°N–25°S, concentrated in Australia, Indonesia and the Philippines, and are extremely rich habitats, giving a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i.
t: Recall the features of coral reefs.

x: Seasonal winds, such as the monsoon, cause seasonal changes in currents, as in the north Indian Ocean.
t: Recall the controls of ocean currents.

x: Ocean currents are horizontal movements that affect climate, fisheries and navigation. Tides are vertical changes in level.
t: Discriminate currents, tides and waves.

x: Both are true and R explains A: at new and full moon the Sun, Earth and Moon line up, adding their pull and giving the largest tidal range.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: The Agulhas runs off south-east Africa, the Benguela off south-west Africa, the Humboldt off western South America and the Gulf Stream in the North Atlantic, giving a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i.
t: Recall the location of each current.

x: I, II and III are correct: winds drive surface water, temperature changes density and coastlines deflect currents. IV is false because tides do move ocean water.
t: Check for a denial of a known cause.

x: Option C is incorrect: the Benguela flows off south-west Africa, not north-west. The Canary is the north-west African current.
t: Check the coast of each current.

x: Both are true: currents shape climate, fisheries and navigation, and a tsunami is a long-wavelength destructive wave.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: Three are warm: Agulhas, Brazil and Gulf Stream. Benguela, Canary and Labrador are cold.
t: Discriminate warm from cold currents.

x: All five are correct: waves are wind-driven oscillations that transfer energy at variable times, while tsunamis have other causes.
t: Recall the features of waves.

x: Both are true but R does not explain A: being periodic describes tides; the Moon's and Sun's gravity causes the rise and fall.
t: Check whether R is the cause or a property.

x: All five are correct: currents are continuous flows driven by density and pressure differences, deflected by the Coriolis force and steered by floor relief.
t: Recall the controls of ocean currents.
s: Consider the following statements about ocean currents: I. Ocean currents are continuous directed movements of water. II. Density differences drive ocean currents. III. The Coriolis force deflects ocean currents. IV. Pressure differences drive ocean currents. V. Ocean-floor configuration influences ocean currents.
o: I, II, III, IV and V

x: Both are true: currents are fairly continuous, and their effects depend on direction and whether they are warm or cold.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: Spring tides have the largest range at new or full moon when pulls add up; neap tides have the smallest range at the quarters when pulls partly cancel, giving a-iii, b-i, c-ii, d-iv.
t: Discriminate spring from neap tides.

x: Both are true and R explains A: waves are linked with coastal erosion because erosion is one of their main effects.
t: Check whether R restates A.

x: Tides are linked with tidal energy. Continuous flow describes currents and oscillation describes waves.
t: Discriminate currents, tides and waves.

x: All five are correct: the Coriolis effect deflects water, salinity and temperature set density that drives deep circulation, floor relief guides currents and air pressure moves surface water.
t: Recall the controls of ocean currents.

x: Both are true: warm currents usually start in low latitudes and cold currents in high latitudes.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: Both are true but R does not explain A: cold currents cooling coasts is a parallel fact, not why warm currents warm them.
t: Check whether R is the cause or a parallel fact.

x: The Mozambique Current is warm and flows through the Mozambique Channel in the Indian Ocean.
t: Recall the location of each current.

x: The Brazil Current is warm and flows south along the east coast of Brazil.
t: Recall the location of each current.

x: All four are correct: the North Atlantic Drift carries warm water toward Europe and continues as the warm Norwegian Current along Norway.
t: Recall the warm currents of the North Atlantic.
